route_has_no_emission_or_execution_stage: This profile is check-only: an admitted epoch is a checked accounting statement about declared shapes, so the driver publishes it with c_source: None and reference_observation: None. c_emission, native_execution, task/mutex/sequential stages and legacy_c_twin are structurally absent for the `epoch` route. native_sanitized and proof are never `not_applicable` under schema 2 and stay `unassessed`: this card adds no sanitized run and claims no per-case proof stage.
lean_is_adjacent_evidence_not_a_stage: proof/QCore/EpochSourceLowering.lean carries 37 audited theorems, including the CT35 and CT36 declarations as worked Lean examples (twoReaders, twoStages) and the CT38 credit refusal and CT39 latency claim. Those model the declaration form, not the fixture bytes, and there is no digest tying the Lean transcription to the fixture. `proof` therefore stays `unassessed` for all four cases, matching the wave-5 discipline of not claiming a stage the executed evidence does not carry.

CT35.scenario: One shared 4096-byte allocation read by two tasks
CT35.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two workers each declare `read page;` for one `let page = share 4096;` cell. The lowering names one cell identity, so the checker's shared entry union counts 4096 once and the published epoch peak is 4096 + (1024 + 1024) + (512 + 2*128) = 6912. The two_cells control declares a second distinct 4096-byte cell both workers read and measures 8192, so the union counts identities rather than readers. The repeated_entry control names the same cell twice in one worker and is refused at Q630 DuplicateSharedEntry rather than deduplicated. Declared footprints, declared runtime overhead and disjoint shared cells remain premises of FlatEpochBoundV1; nothing here imports a footprint from C or from a run.

CT36.expected: Bound at least 8192 plus modeled overhead
CT36.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two independent workers declare `peak 3072;` and `peak 5120;`. Because every assignment of phases to independent tasks is an admitted configuration, the peaks are summed rather than maximized: the published concurrent private peak is 8192 and the epoch peak is 8192 + (512 + 2*128) = 8960, at least the summed peaks plus the modeled overhead. Two controls straddle the summed figure with the same two peaks: an allocation of 8192 is admitted and 8191 is refused with the ordered cascade [Q637, Q638]. A maximized reading would have called 5120 the peak and admitted both, so the refusal is what makes the summing falsifiable. The overhead figures are a declared premise; a `measured RUNS` suffix in their place is Q640 (exercised elsewhere in the same test file).

controls.compiler/tests/fixtures/ct/CT36/summed_a: accepted; allocation 8192 exactly covers the summed peak
controls.compiler/tests/fixtures/ct/CT36/maximize: refused; ordered cascade ["Q637", "Q638"] one byte below the summed peak

CT38.scenario: Child credit splits total more than original credit
CT38.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: two children each declare `credit 6144 effort 100;` out of an epoch that declares `bound 8192 effort 1000;`. Each child's own demand fits its own credit, so no per-task check refuses it; the granted total 12288 exceeds the 8192 allocation and the exact ordered cascade is [Q637] CreditsExceedAllocation on the memory axis. The control splits the same total within it (4096 + 4096 = 8192) and is admitted with granted_credits.memory = allocation.memory = 8192, so the refusal is keyed to the sum and not to the split.

CT39.scenario: Concurrent work bound used as wall-clock bound
CT39.semantic_profile: source.epoch.bound.v1: a well-accounted epoch additionally writes `bound effort as latency;`, asking for its work bound as a completion time. The driver derives and rechecks the bound first and only then puts the claim to the profile's own epoch_wall_clock_bound, which always refuses: the exact ordered cascade is [Q639] WallClockUnavailable. The control is the same epoch without the claim: admitted, with work_total on the effort axis = 800 and EpochAssumption::NoScheduleModel on the certificate, so a consumer cannot drop the premise and read the total as a finish time. There is no core count, queueing or preemption anywhere in this profile.

controls.compiler/tests/fixtures/ct/CT39/work_bou: accepted; work_total.effort = 800, NoScheduleModel present, epoch_wall_clock_bound still refuses on the published certificate

epoch_bound_check.note: The bound is derived and rechecked before the claim is refused, so Q639 is measured against a certificate the checker really issued.
